# A handler a component's body writes, assigning to an index that reads a
# prop, writes what each call site handed it. The optimizer splices such a
# body where a constant prop folds a branch away, and its copy shared the
# assignment's target with the declaration, so the first splice's argument
# was written into the declaration and every later copy wrote under the
# first one's key -- the Pokédex's names, all filed under the slug of a type
# on a page the test never opened.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

var written map[string, int] = {}

component tally(kind string, word string) ui.node {
    if kind == "a" {
        effect(@mount { written["a/{word}"] = 1 })
    } else {
        effect(@mount { written["b/{word}"] = 2 })
    }
    ui.text(value=word)
}

component pair ui.node {
    var first = "fig"
    var second = "kiwi"

    tally(kind="a", word=first)
    tally(kind="b", word=second)
}

func testEachCopyWritesItsOwnKey(t test.Test, c pair) {
    t.assert(written.get("a/fig", 0) == 1)
    t.assert(written.get("b/kiwi", 0) == 2)
    t.assert(written.length() == 2)
}

ui.window {
    pair
}
